decision: AIGVDBench defines real videos as a matched real-video pool paired to generated videos by prompt; it does not establish camera-origin labels. OpenVid is multi-upstream in-the-wild video with filtering, so source provenance and negative-label semantics remain weaker than camera-source claims.

primary_findings.fact: AIGVDBench reports 31 generation methods: 20 open-source and 11 closed-source; open-source methods use 20,000 generated videos split 14k/3k/3k, with 20,000 real videos paired by the same prompt and partitioned identically.

Closed-source methods use 2,000 generated test videos and a matched real-video test set formed by selecting the first 2,000 from the complete real-video test set; this is a benchmark construction rule, not proof of camera origin.
The paper states OpenVid-HD is selected as the source of real videos for balanced prompt selection; content/source selection remains a dataset-pipeline property.

OpenVid-1M/OpenVidHD is an in-the-wild multi-upstream collection (ChronoMagic, CelebVHQ, Open-Sora-plan and Panda subset) with quality, temporal consistency, motion and clarity filtering; the paper does not make every clip a verified camera-origin sample.
Dataset card exposes cc-by-4.0 and 14k/3k/3k splits with Video_id and Video_Prompts; this supports release-level access metadata, not per-sample label/ancestor/time/license evidence.
